disease_label_per_paper: Addison's disease presenting as acute renal failure and hyperkalemic paralysis with adrenal crisis
presentation_summary: 37-year-old man presented with acute weakness and inability to move his limbs after waking from sleep, with similar milder episodes after prolonged rest in the past.
He denied recent medication or drug use, diarrhea, infections, trauma, and significant past medical history.
On emergency-department arrival BP was 98/50 mmHg and HR 84/min. Exam showed weakness in all four limbs, intact sensation, no fecal or urinary incontinence, and inability to walk.

While history was being taken and labs drawn, he had cardiac arrest. ECG showed sinus rhythm with PR prolongation and QRS widening; he was intubated and resuscitated with return of spontaneous circulation after 6 minutes.
Pre-arrest labs showed potassium 8.8 mmol/L, sodium 124 mmol/L, creatinine 1.7 mg/dL, BUN 32 mg/dL, glucose 76 mg/dL, and chloride 99 mmol/L.

He underwent emergent renal replacement therapy for life-threatening hyperkalemia, then CRRT for oligoanuric renal failure and hemodynamic instability. Weakness resolved and he was extubated by hospital day 4.

actual_treatment: intubation and resuscitation after cardiac arrest with ROSC after 6 minutes
emergent renal replacement therapy for life-threatening hyperkalemia
continuous renal replacement therapy over the next 4 days for oligoanuric renal failure with hemodynamic instability
maintenance hydrocortisone 10 mg twice daily at discharge
education on stress-dose hydrocortisone three times usual dose in febrile illness
emergency injectable hydrocortisone vial for vomiting or inability to take pills

outcome.clinical_course: Potassium normalized on CRRT, weakness resolved, he was extubated on hospital day 4, and discharged on hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone with emergency stress-dose instructions.
outcome.source_text_value: His potassium levels gradually came back to normal levels on CRRT. He made a steady recovery and was off RRT and extubated on the fourth day of hospitalisation. By this time, his weakness had completely resolved.
